notes:
2026-09-16 (AI-fact-elimination sweep, card-results lane): re-examined the 2 remaining unprovenanced facts (source `sacrifice` + its paired sink, both `target:{types:{has:['Legendary','Creature']}}`) fact-by-fact, per the standing 'attempt hard before declaring bespoke' instruction — did NOT just accept the pre-existing 2026-09-12 knownGaps note at face value. `apply-recognizers.mjs louisoix-s-sacrifice` rerun: 0 new facts; the run's own output directly confirms `sacrifice-effect-structural`'s own suppressed 'recognizer-exception' decline is still exactly accurate today (tried `\bsacrifice (?:a|an) creature\b`, 0 matches, because the real text's next word after 'sacrifice a' is 'legendary', not 'creature'). Independently confirmed via direct code read (`card.ts`'s own `kind:'sacrifice'` Effect type, lines ~492-503) that `validType` is a genuinely closed union (`'creature'|'artifact'|'enchantment'|'any'|'creature-or-artifact'`) with NO subtype/legendary-narrowing field anywhere (unlike `move`'s own `subtype` array) — this is a real, still-open, structural vocabulary gap, not just a permanently-accepted approximation. **Recognizer + engine-core escalation** (upgrading the existing knownGaps note from 'accepted trade-off' to 'real, closeable, single-card-confirmed gap'): `card.ts`'s `sacrifice` Effect needs a way to narrow the sacrificed object by the Legendary supertype (either a new `validType` member, e.g. `'legendary-creature'`, or a `subtype`-style field mirroring `move`'s own) before `sacrifice-effect-structural.ts` could build a 'sacrifice a legendary creature' template and close both this card's remaining facts (source + paired sink) in one shot. Checked whole-pool for other real motivators: `louisoix-s-sacrifice` is the ONLY card combining `kind:'sacrifice'` with any legendary-subtype text today (grepped every `definition.ts` for both 'legendary' and `kind: 'sacrifice'` together) — single-card, but the same accepted single-card bar `lifegainDoubleKeyword-structural.ts`/`ptFormulaSetToCreaturesControlled-structural.ts` already establish elsewhere in this catalog, not a reason to defer. `verify-synergy.mjs` (scoped): 0 hard failures (OK). `verify-text-coverage.mjs` (scoped): 69% — the one real uncovered span is the leading "As an additional cost to cast this spell," clause fragment (not a NEW gap; same already-approximated sacrifice clause, the annotation only anchors starting at 'sacrifice', not the full sentence prefix). `review` stays "ai" (already "ai", no content change made). Prior 2026-09-12: migrated to the unified Fact/annotations model. Real oracle text (data/fin/fin_scryfall.json, collector_number 59): "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a legendary creature or pay {2}.\nCounter target activated ability, triggered ability, or noncreature spell." Mana cost {U}, type line 'Instant' — both verified, unchanged from definition.ts.

Baseline self-cast/self-graveyard pair ({event:'cast', from:'Hand', target:'self'} / {to:'Graveyard', subject:'self'}), both typeLine-anchored on 'Instant' — mirrors restoration-magic's/fate-of-the-sun-cryst's own real Instant baseline (no self-enters/self-dies for a spell, only cast+graveyard).

Sacrifice-as-additional-cost modeled as ONE merged SOURCE fact, not a bare ACT tag: {event:'sacrifice', from:'Battlefield', to:'Graveyard', controller:'you', target:{types:{has:['Legendary','Creature']}}, targeted:true} — sacrificing a legendary creature you control (not self) is a guaranteed, unpreventable movement with no separate consequence fact already covering it on this card, so it gets zoneFrom/zoneTo inline per the standing ACT-vs-CONSEQUENCE table (SYNERGY_DESIGN.md), same as self-cast's own Hand->Stack. `targeted:true` since choosing WHICH legendary creature (when you control more than one) is a real bucket-of-candidates choice, informational only. The 'OR pay {2}' alternative cost is NOT modeled as a fact — mana payment isn't normally factored, and it produces no distinguishing effect of its own (same singular counter effect either way). Companion SINK fact (wants a legendary creature present as cost fodder) narrowed from the old schema's untyped {types:{has:['Creature']}} to {to:'Battlefield', controller:'you', types:{has:['Legendary','Creature']}} — a real correctness fix (the old fact only checked for ANY creature, not specifically a legendary one); confirmed via find-synergies.mjs this costs zero real matches (every producer that satisfied the old untyped want in this pool is itself already a real Legendary creature).

Counter effect: {event:'counter', target:{}, targeted:true} — reuses the already-promoted, already-real `counter` vocabulary (card.ts's own log-only CounterEffect/interfaces.ts's `counter()`, added when this card was first authored 2026-09-06) — no new engine work needed. `target:{}` (empty Constraints = genuinely unrestricted) + `targeted:true` mirrors restoration-magic's own real CR 601.2c-targeted-but-vocabulary-can't-narrow-further pattern (there is no 'ability'/'spell'-vs-'permanent' distinction in this model's Constraints vocabulary, and no stack/object model at all — see interfaces.ts's own `counter` doc comment — so 'noncreature spell' vs. 'activated/triggered ability' can't be encoded any more precisely than 'a real target exists'). This is the ONLY card in the pool declaring `event:'counter'` in either role (grepped) — a documented, real gap: no payoff card wants a countered-spell event yet, and activated/triggered-ability countering specifically has zero possible engine representation (no Stack/ability-object model exists here at all), so the fact is honestly bare rather than overclaiming a target shape the engine can't check.

Real, pre-existing 'not mocked' bug fixed in the same pass (this migration is the flagged 'revisit case-by-case' touch SYNERGY_DESIGN.md's 2026-09-12 PlayerState.creatureCards entry already calls out for this exact card): the old scenario tagged the shared GENERIC_FILLER_CREATURE ('Grizzly Bears') with `creatureSubtypes:['Legendary']` — a real card that isn't legendary, mislabeled. Replaced with `creatureCards:[{name:'Stiltzkin, Moogle Merchant', subtypes:['Legendary','Moogle'], power:1, toughness:2}]` (data/fin/fin_scryfall.json: {W} Legendary Creature — Moogle, 1/2) — a real, specifically-named legendary creature, same `creatureCards` mechanism Phoenix Down's own fix established. Note: this engine's own `hasSubtype('Legendary')` pragmatic-supertype-as-subtype convention (documented on aerith-gainsborough's own definition.ts, since Forge tracks Legendary as a real supertype the CardDefinition model here doesn't separately track) is the correct, existing house style — not the bug; the bug was the specific card identity (a real non-legendary Grizzly Bears), not the subtype-array mechanism.

Scenarios trimmed from 2 to 1, per the standing 'basic function, not unit-test coverage' rule (SYNERGY_DESIGN.md, 2026-09-12) and this task's own explicit instruction: this card is NOT a real branching modal for scenario-count purposes (unlike Phoenix Down's genuinely different two modes) — the sacrifice-vs-pay-{2} split is an additional-COST choice, and the spell's own effect (counter) is singular either way; mode 1's 'pay {2} instead' produces no distinguishing trace line (mana payment isn't modeled) so it doesn't need its own scenario. Kept mode 0 (the more demonstrative sacrifice path). `definition.ts` itself is UNCHANGED (still a real `modal`/`ctx.mode` two-branch Effect, since the underlying cost mechanism genuinely has two real payment paths — the scenario-count decision doesn't reopen the effect-modeling shape).

Added 'louisoix-s-sacrifice' to scripts/annotation-coverage.mjs's ANNOTATED_CARD_SLUGS. Regenerated trace.json via run-scenarios.mjs (1 scenario; real fn:'cast'/'read:isCreature'/'sacrifice'/'counter'/'move' trace lines). verify-synergy.mjs: scoped OK (0 hard failures); full pool 317 v2 cards checked, 9 hard failures, all pre-existing/concurrent-session work unrelated to this card (cargo-ship, cecil-dark-knight-cecil-redeemed-paladin, dragoon-s-wyvern, ice-flan, il-mheg-pixie, stiltzkin-moogle-merchant, the-wind-crystal, white-auracite, zack-fair — confirmed none reference louisoix-s-sacrifice). vitest run functional-model: 238/238. find-synergies.mjs real isolated before/after diff (git-stash swap of just this card's own synergy.json/scenarios.ts/trace.json, full pool run both times): the exact same ~90 producer lines into Louisoix's Sacrifice (battlefield-presence/enters-the-battlefield legendary creatures) are byte-identical before and after — zero lines gained or lost despite the sink's added Legendary constraint (every one of those producers is itself already a real Legendary creature in this pool); Louisoix's Sacrifice's own 13 outbound 'moves to graveyard'/13 'dies' matches (renamed from the old schema's 'graveyard presence'/'dies' labels, same set of cards) are also unchanged. `event:'counter'`/`event:'sacrifice'` (the new/promoted-vocabulary facts): 0 matches either direction, expected (no sink in the pool wants either event yet — same 'promotes vocabulary, doesn't itself create a match' outcome every other event promotion in this file has seen).
knownGaps: `sacrifice`'s own `validType` vocabulary has no 'legendary' subtype filter (only creature/artifact/enchantment/token-or-not/creature-or-artifact) — approximated as `validType:'creature'` at the engine level (card.ts), same nearest-available-vocabulary trade-off `destroy`'s own `nonLand` already accepts elsewhere. The FACT itself is honestly narrowed to Legendary+Creature (verify-synergy.mjs's forward zone-evidence check only verifies the `to`/`from`/`controller` triple, not the `target` type filter, so this approximation doesn't need or get a verify-synergy exemption). UPDATED 2026-09-16: re-classified from 'accepted trade-off' to a real, open, single-card-confirmed recognizer+engine-core escalation — see this file's own 2026-09-16 notes entry for the exact `card.ts` field addition that would close both of this card's own remaining unprovenanced facts (source `sacrifice` + its paired sink).

`counter` has no real target to remove (no stack/ability/spell object model exists in this engine at all) — a real logged event, not a fabricated state mutation. The 'activated ability, triggered ability, or noncreature spell' scope can't be encoded any more precisely than a bare, unrestricted `target:{}` — there is no Constraints vocabulary for 'kind of stack object' (spell vs. activated ability vs. triggered ability), and no other pool card declares `event:'counter'` yet to have forced that vocabulary into existence. Any future card needing a REAL countered-object reference, or a real counterspell-payoff card wanting `event:'counter'`, would need actual engine/vocabulary work beyond this.
